ai_summary: Great Britain's wind fleet is currently generating 17.1 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 5.9 GW, accounting for 58.4% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This strong renewable generation has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in sharp contrast to the GB-wide average of 77 gCO2/kWh. However, because cross-border transmission infrastructure cannot accommodate this northern surplus, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 18.4 GWh at a constraint cost of about £1,009,392 through Balancing Mechanism bids. Annualizing this daily expenditure indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £368 million, which increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £1/MWh. To compensate for this stranded green electricity, fossil fuel plants elsewhere on the network were dispatched, resulting in an estimated 3,503,980 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and emitting an additional 6,455 tonnes of CO2. These figures underscore the severe financial and ecological consequences of grid bottlenecks, which leave consumers paying substantial constraint fees to switch off clean generation while simultaneously funding replacement carbon emissions south of the border.
